classification.difficultyReason: Recombine unequal shaded pieces into comparable areas; the circle diagram requires pairing semicircles with complementary outside-circle regions to recover whole squares.

content.prompt: For each of the diagrams shown, work out what fraction of the rectangle is shaded.

spec.description: Six equal squares in a horizontal strip, retaining each diagonal, vertical, triangular or horizontal partition and its source shaded side.
spec.mathematics: Each square is half shaded, including the fourth square's triangle and the fifth square's combined top and bottom triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Required shading is visible; the fraction answer is absent.

answer.worked:
Half of each of the six equal squares is shaded. The shaded area is therefore 3 whole squares out of 6.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Shaded fraction}&=\frac36\\&=\frac12\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Six equal squares arranged in three two-square panels, retaining all vertical boundaries, the first diagonal, middle parallelogram and final triangular partitions.
spec.mathematics: The shaded areas in the three panels equal half a square, one square and half a square respectively, totalling two of six squares.
spec.answerVisibility: Required shading is visible; the fraction answer is absent.

answer.worked:
The first pair contains two shaded quarter-squares, making half a square. The middle shaded parallelogram equals one square. The last shaded triangle equals half a square.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Shaded fraction}&=\frac{\frac12+1+\frac12}{6}\\&=\frac26\\&=\frac13\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two adjacent equal squares with centre lines, diagonals and centred half-side inner squares. Two outer trapezoids are shaded on the left, and two inner triangles on the right.
spec.mathematics: The left shading occupies 3/8 of one square and the right shading 1/8 of one square, totalling half a square in a two-square rectangle.
spec.answerVisibility: The fraction answer is absent; required shaded regions remain visible.

answer.worked:
The two shaded trapezoids cover $\frac38$ of the left square. The two shaded triangles cover $\frac18$ of the right square. Together they cover half of one square, while the rectangle contains two equal squares.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Shaded fraction}&=\frac{\frac38+\frac18}{2}\\&=\frac14\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A two-row, four-column square grid containing the source semicircles, white circles, shaded circle exteriors and one fully shaded square.
spec.mathematics: The four shaded semicircles make two whole circles. Together with the two shaded circle exteriors, these make two squares; the fully shaded square makes three of eight squares.
spec.answerVisibility: Required shading is visible; no supplied answer is printed.

answer.worked: The four shaded semicircles make two whole circles. Combining them with the two shaded regions outside circles makes two complete squares. Including the fully shaded square gives 3 shaded squares out of 8, so the fraction is $\frac38$.
